subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What contract should ClawHub enforce for source metadata supplied to `clawhub skill publish`: separately labeled unverified attribution, rejection/deprecation in favor of the trusted GitHub-import path, or server verification that can create sourceProvenance?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current separation is deliberate, but the repository does not establish whether the accepted client claims should be retained, exposed, rejected, or verified; choosing among those outcomes changes the public trust model and compatibility contract.

options.title: Separate Unverified Attribution
options.body: Persist the claims in a clearly named unverified field, label them visibly, and prohibit them from affecting verify results or trusted Skill Card signals.

options.title: Trusted Import Only
options.body: Deprecate or reject skill publish source flags and direct publishers to the existing server-managed GitHub-backed import workflow for provenance.

options.title: Verify CLI Claims
options.body: Add server-side repository, commit, path, and artifact matching before storing the claims as trusted sourceProvenance.

recommendation.title: Separate Unverified Attribution
recommendation.body: Persist the claims in a clearly named unverified field, label them visibly, and prohibit them from affecting verify results or trusted Skill Card signals.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the trusted GitHub-backed source and verification architecture that this decision must preserve or extend.
